tasks.title: The severity predicate that grades a round under the resolved policy
tasks.acceptance: One engine predicate over (rows, policy): under `all` clean iff no non-PASS row; under `blocking` clean iff no non-PASS row carries a blocking severity, where `error` blocks and a severity outside the enum, JSON null, an absent key or a non-string value all block. Four fixtures, one per unrecognised shape; the mutant that must fail is grading a row with no usable severity as advisory. Section 7 rows 5, 6, 7 and 8 pass.
tasks.closed_reason:
- One engine predicate over (rows, policy): engine.AuditRowsClean(rows []map[string]any, convergeOn string) bool in internal/engine/auditclean.go, a pure function of its two arguments because section 2 stamps clean at record time rather than recomputing it live.
- Under all, clean iff the round holds no non-PASS row: the loop returns false on the first row AuditRowIsPass rejects, and any policy literal other than the exact string blocking takes that arm, so an unrefused value grades under the stricter default.
- Under blocking, clean iff no non-PASS row carries a blocking severity: auditSeverityBlocking names the advisory half of the vocabulary (warning, info) and blocks by exclusion, so error blocks and a string outside the enum, JSON null, an absent key and a non-string value all block. The comparison is byte-for-byte like AuditRowIsPass, so WARNING is outside the enum and blocks, which keeps section 4 identity error plus unrecognised equals the blocking rows true. It never consults engine.SeverityRank, which is built for the review words and ranks every audit severity unknown.
- Four fixtures, one per unrecognised shape: TestAuditRowsClean_UnusableSeverityBlocks subtests a string outside the enum, JSON null, an absent key, and a value that is not a string, each unclean under blocking and under all.
- The mutant that must fail is grading a row with no usable severity as advisory: built as blocking iff the severity type assertion equals error, and run. It reddened exactly the four row-8 subtests at auditclean_test.go:77, the blocking assertion, while rows 5, 6 and 7 stayed green. Three further named mutants were run for discrimination: grade on status alone reddened rows 5 and 6 only; return clean whenever the policy is blocking reddened rows 7 and 8 only; special-case info only reddened row 6 alone, which is why section 7 asserts it apart from row 5. The real implementation then turned all six functions and four subtests green.
- Section 7 rows 5, 6, 7 and 8 pass: TestAuditRowsClean_InfoIsAdvisory, _WarningIsAdvisory, _ErrorBlocksUnderBoth and _UnusableSeverityBlocks all PASS, plus _PassRowsAreNotGraded (PASS rows carry severity null, so a predicate over rows of any severity would report every all-PASS round unclean) and _UnknownPolicyGradesAsAll.
- Quality gate green: check-suite-state.sh, golangci-lint run with 0 issues, check-deadcode.sh and check-complexity.sh all passed, exit 0.

tasks.title: The unattended change-rule fence at every write path
tasks.acceptance: Under TP_UNATTENDED=1 a write that changes the resolved value to blocking exits 2 at tp set --workflow, its --project form, tp import and tp config --extract; a write of all, a --project write of blocking beneath a task override of all, and an import carrying an already-resolved blocking forward all pass. The fence is string-shaped and placed before the type dispatch, not a widening of the numeric fence. Every test sets the variable it names rather than relying on the ambient value. Section 7 rows 12, 13, 13b and 13c pass.
tasks.closed_reason:
Section 3's change rule is implemented at all four write paths and proved by running.

- tp set --workflow audit_converge_on=blocking exits 2 under TP_UNATTENDED=1 when it changes what resolves, leaving the task file byte-identical.
- Its --project form exits 2 on the same terms and creates no .tp/config.json.
- tp import exits 2, placed after the exists-guard and after the workflow-preservation step, so it compares the block that will actually be written.
- tp config --extract calls the rule over every scanned base before the merge; the refusing input does not exist yet and that was measured, not reasoned (see the note below), so only the passing half is asserted.
- A write of all passes at both set sinks, including over an already-resolved blocking, which tightens the gate.
- A --project write of blocking beneath a task override of all passes: the value reaches the project layer and all still resolves.
- An import carrying an already-resolved blocking forward passes, which is the case a field- or value-scoped fence would deadlock for ever.
- The fence is string-shaped and its call sites sit in the string-enum arm before the integer and float dispatch; the numeric fenceWorkflowWrite is untouched, since its float64 signature runs after the literal is parsed as a number.
- Every test decides TP_UNATTENDED for its own child through a runner that filters the variable out of os.Environ() and re-adds it only when the arm needs it; row 13c removes it rather than omitting it.
- Rows 12, 13, 13b and 13c pass, and seven mutants were built and run in rsync copies against a baseline binary from the unmutated tree: all seven fail. The two the spec names no row for -- an import fence reading the active pointer instead of its own target, and a rule refusing any change rather than a change to blocking -- both survived the first matrix and are now killed by two added tests.

Gate green: check-suite-state.sh, golangci-lint, check-deadcode.sh, check-complexity.sh, exit 0. Under TP_UNATTENDED=1 the cli package's failing set is byte-identical to HEAD's 21 pre-existing failures (TestImport_WorkflowPreserved's three subtests among them); three tests this fence broke under the ambient variable now state their own environment. Out of scope and reported: --extract's widened scope, the refusal's three exits, and the escalate enum value, so the hint still says --decision other.
